findings.issue_text: [BUG] `organization_context.member.has_global_access` references a variable `organization_context` that is never defined anywhere in this endpoint's `get` method (the diff context shows only `request` and `queryset` in scope), so every request to this endpoint raises NameError and returns a 500. The audit logs endpoint crashes with NameError on every call — not just the optimized path — because the `or` expression is evaluated before the `use_optimized` gate short-circuits it; the entire endpoint becomes unusable, not just the new feature.

[BUG] The comment's assumption that 'the underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically' is false: `list(queryset[start_offset:stop])` with a negative `start_offset` raises Django's `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported`, so the new advanced-negative-offset branch in both `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` and the modified `CursorPaginator.get_result` crashes whenever `cursor.offset < 0`. Any request carrying a negative cursor offset (which `Cursor.offset = int(offset)` in src/sentry/utils/cursors.py now accepts without validation, e.g. via a crafted `cursor=0:-5:0` query parameter) raises AssertionError → 500 instead of a 4xx; the enabled 'advanced feature' path is unimplementable against a Django QuerySet as written.

[BUG] `self.paginate(...)` is called with `enable_advanced_features=True`, but the paginate mixin does not accept or forward arbitrary keyword arguments to the paginator constructor, so the optimized branch raises `TypeError: paginate() got an unexpected keyword argument 'enable_advanced_features'` instead of instantiating `OptimizedCursorPaginator` with that flag. The first request with `optimized_pagination=true` from an authorized admin returns a 500; the new paginator path can never be exercised successfully even after the NameError above is fixed.

[BUG] `OptimizedCursorPaginator` subclasses `BasePaginator` and relies on `self.key`, `self.desc`, `self.max_limit`, `self.build_queryset`, `self.count_hits`, and `self.post_query_filter`, which are attributes/methods of `CursorPaginator`, not of the base class — instantiating this paginator with `order_by='-datetime'` fails because the order_by parsing that sets `self.key`/`self.desc` lives in `CursorPaginator.__init__`. Even if the call-site kwargs issue were fixed, `get_result` raises AttributeError on `self.key`/`self.build_queryset` because `BasePaginator.__init__` does not parse `order_by` into `key`/`desc`; the class as written cannot function.

[BUG] `val["end_timestamp_precise"]` is a required key access, so any span event already on the ingest topic (or produced by a relay/ingest version that predates this field) raises KeyError, crashing the consumer batch. During rolling deploy and for the retention window of pre-existing Kafka messages, the spans processing consumer raises KeyError and the batch fails/retries indefinitely, stalling partition consumption — the diff assumes all in-flight data already carries the field, which no deployment ordering can guarantee.

[ADVISORY] The Lua script fully converts span set keys to sorted sets (zcard/zunionstore), so any remaining reader or writer in the codebase still touching these keys with set commands (sadd/sscan/scard/sunionstore outside this diff, e.g. other flush/trim paths in spans/buffer.py) will hit Redis WRONGTYPE errors the moment the new writer runs. Deploy skew or any un-migrated code path interacting with `span-buf:s:*` keys raises ResponseError WRONGTYPE, silently failing span buffering until all readers are converted; verify every reader of these keys was migrated in the same change.

[ADVISORY] The modified `CursorPaginator.get_result` line `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` allows a negative offset on prev cursors, feeding a negative slice index into the queryset where the only guard is the crash in the advanced branch — the shared code path was made reachable-negative without any validation. A client-supplied prev cursor with negative offset slices the queryset with a negative start, raising Django's negative-indexing AssertionError on the legacy (non-optimized) path too; the change to the default paginator is unrelated to the stated spans-buffer purpose of this PR and widens the crash surface for existing endpoints.

[BUG] process_batch reads val["end_timestamp_precise"] unconditionally, so any span event on the topic produced by an old producer (or lacking the field) raises KeyError and kills processing of the batch. During a rolling deploy, messages serialized before this code ships crash the consumer batch instead of being skipped; use of .get with a default (e.g. timestamp) would avoid hard data-loss/ poisoning of the partition.

[BUG] Span is a NamedTuple and the new required field end_timestamp_precise is inserted before is_segment_span, shifting every positional construction of Span. Any call site constructing Span positionally (outside the tests updated here) now binds is_segment_span's positional value to end_timestamp_precise, silently producing wrong is_segment_span flags or a TypeError; positional constructions were valid before this diff.

[BUG] The OptimizedCursorPaginator negative-offset branch slices queryset[start_offset:stop] with a negative start_offset, which Django rejects: QuerySet slicing raises AssertionError ('Negative indexing is not supported') for negative starts. Any request with optimized_pagination=true and a cursor carrying a negative offset returns a 500 instead of a page; the code comment claiming 'the underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically' is factually wrong.

[BUG] enable_advanced checks organization_context.member.has_global_access without guarding member being None (superusers can lack an OrganizationMember), raising AttributeError on the member access. A superuser requesting optimized_pagination=true on an org where they have no membership gets a 500 instead of falling back to the standard paginator branch.

[BUG] The redirect-resolution loop limit is silently lowered from 10000 to 1000, so parent chains deeper than 1000 now exit the loop without joining, a correctness regression the removed comment explicitly acknowledged as a known tradeoff. Deep segment trees longer than 1000 no longer merge into the correct set; their spans land in a stale set_key and are flushed attached to the wrong parent, with no metric or log marking the bail-out.

[BUG] The zpopmin eviction (span_count > 1000) silently drops evicted spans with no metric, log, or record, and evicts by oldest end_timestamp_precise regardless of whether the evicted span is still needed by the flusher's parent/child reconstruction. Spans past the cap are permanently deleted before flush and the loss is invisible: no spans.buffer.evicted metric exists to alert on, so operators cannot distinguish capacity pressure from a processing bug.

[ADVISORY] The max_segment_spans guard (count-based skip with its own metric 'spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded') was deleted and replaced only by the byte-size check, removing the count-exceeded safety path. Segments composed of many tiny spans now pass the byte check but can exceed the previously enforced span-count ceiling; the deleted metric disappears, so that failure signal is gone from dashboards.

[ADVISORY] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result is a near-verbatim copy of BasePaginator/CursorPaginator.get_result (~90 duplicated lines) differing only in the negative-offset branch. The next fix to cursor arithmetic (e.g. build_cursor handling, prev-cursor off-by-one) must be applied in two hand-maintained copies; the deletion test fails — subclassing and overriding only the slicing block would make the duplicated body unnecessary.

[ADVISORY] New admin-only pagination behavior is gated on the raw query param optimized_pagination == "true" with no feature flag or options entry, so it cannot be disabled without a code deploy and is user-controllable via URL. If the optimized path misbehaves in production, operators must roll back code rather than flip a flag; meanwhile any admin can enable the untested path at will by editing the URL.

[ADVISORY] No test in this diff covers the new eviction path (zpopmin when span_count > 1000) or the zadd/zscan conversion with duplicate payloads and distinct scores; all updated tests use four spans against a 1000 cap, so the headline feature of the PR is untested. A regression in the eviction logic (e.g. popping the just-inserted span, or off-by-one leaving the set unbounded) would ship undetected; the PR's stated purpose — 'eviction during insert' — has zero assertions.

[ADVISORY] The shared BasePaginator.get_result slicing is modified (start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset) as part of a feature intended only for the audit-log endpoint, changing slicing behavior for every paginator subclass sharing this code path. All other endpoints using this paginator inherit the changed prev-cursor arithmetic; if any caller relies on the prior expression for is_prev cursors, page boundaries shift silently with no test in the diff covering non-audit-log paginators.

[BUG] OptimizedCursorPaginator's negative-offset branch slices the queryset with a negative start (queryset[cursor.offset:stop]), which Django's QuerySet.set_limits rejects with AssertionError: 'Negative indexing is not supported', so every request that reaches this branch returns a 500 instead of paginated results. Any admin passing optimized_pagination=true with a negative cursor offset crashes the audit-log endpoint with a 500; the comment's claim that 'the underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically' is false.

[ADVISORY] The audit-log endpoint changes (OptimizedCursorPaginator switch, optimized_pagination query param, admin gating) are entirely unrelated to the stated PR intent of spans-buffer insertion/eviction and are not traceable to any requirement in this change. Scope drift couples an experimental, crash-prone paginator to a stable audit endpoint; reviewers and bisects of the span-buffer work now must reason about API pagination behavior, and the experimental path is one query-param away from production users.

[ADVISORY] The shared BasePaginator/CursorPaginator.get_result silently changes slicing semantics for ALL paginated endpoints (start_offset = max(0, offset) for non-prev cursors), not just the new optimized path. Any existing caller that legitimately passes a negative or unusual offset gets clamped to 0 with no requirement in this diff calling for shared-paginator behavior changes; results silently differ from prior releases across every paginated API.

[BUG] OptimizedCursorPaginator extends BasePaginator but its get_result dereferences attributes (self.max_limit, self.build_queryset, self.count_hits, self.desc, self.key, self.post_query_filter) that are defined on CursorPaginator, not BasePaginator; instantiating or calling get_result on this class raises AttributeError. The first real request through the optimized path fails with AttributeError instead of paginating, meaning the new endpoint branch was never exercised.

[ADVISORY] The prev-cursor trim condition `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` uses the raw (possibly negative) offset while results were sliced from start_offset, so under the negative-offset feature the trim logic compares against an inconsistent basis and mis-trims prev pages. Admins navigating backwards with negative-offset cursors get duplicated or dropped boundary rows on prev pages.

[ADVISORY] The redirect-chain walk limit is silently lowered from 10000 to 1000 with no requirement or comment, halving the maximum segment-tree depth that can be correctly joined. Traces with parent-redirect chains deeper than 1000 (previously supported, per the deleted comment) will fail to join to their true segment root, misattributing spans — a behavior regression hidden inside an unrelated PR.

[BUG] The max_segment_spans count-cap enforcement (metric, error log, and segment skip) is deleted while the only replacement limit is the Lua-side zpopmin eviction at 1000 members, leaving the flush path with no per-segment span-count bound for keys populated before or outside the eviction path. A segment key that accumulates more than 1000 members via non-evicting writes (e.g. score updates via zadd on existing members, or keys written before deploy) is loaded in full into flush memory; the deleted 'segment_span_count_exceeded' safeguard no longer fires.

[ADVISORY] New behavior is gated on the raw query param `optimized_pagination` with no feature flag or options entry, and the privilege check `organization_context.member.has_global_access` assumes a Member object exists for every authenticated caller. The experimental path cannot be disabled without a code deploy, and callers authenticated without an organization member binding (e.g. certain token/API-key auth paths) hit an AttributeError instead of falling back to the default paginator.

[ADVISORY] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result is a near-verbatim copy of CursorPaginator.get_result (~90 duplicated lines) differing only in the negative-offset branch, a parallel hand-maintained copy of the pagination core. Every future fix to cursor pagination (boundary handling, hits accounting, build_cursor interplay) must now be applied in two places; the two copies have already drifted (max(0, offset) clamp present in both, negative branch only in one).

[ADVISORY] A comment-only change to Cursor.__init__ claims to 'allow negative offsets' but adds no code, implying a behavior change that does not exist in this file. Future readers auditing the negative-offset feature trace the claim here and find no implementation, wasting investigation time and giving false confidence that the cursor layer validates or supports negative offsets.

[BUG] OptimizedCursorPaginator is used with order_by='-datetime' (DateTimePaginator-style datetime keys), but its get_item_key calls math.floor/math.ceil on the item's key value. build_cursor invokes get_item_key on each serialized-adjacent model instance; math.ceil(datetime) raises TypeError, so every request with optimized_pagination=true for a superuser fails with a 500 instead of paginating.

[BUG] The code references `organization_context.member.has_global_access`, but `organization_context` is not defined anywhere in this endpoint's scope (this diff imports no such symbol and the surrounding get() body never binds it). Any request reaching get() raises NameError before pagination, turning the audit-log endpoint into a guaranteed 500 for all callers, not just the optimized path.

[BUG] The negative-offset branch slices `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative start, but Django QuerySets do not support negative slicing (they raise AssertionError 'Negative indexing is not supported'). When enable_advanced_features is on and a client sends a cursor with negative offset, get_result raises AssertionError instead of returning a page — the comment's claim that 'the underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically' is false.

[BUG] In the prev-cursor trimming branch, `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` compares against the raw (possibly negative) offset while results were sliced with that negative offset, so the arithmetic mixes two incompatible offset semantics. For negative-offset prev cursors the trim condition never matches the actual slice length, so the boundary row is either duplicated or dropped on prev-page navigation.

[BUG] process_batch now requires `val["end_timestamp_precise"]` unconditionally, but the ingest-spans schema/producer was not changed in this diff to guarantee the field. Any in-flight or legacy message lacking the key (e.g. during a rolling deploy, or from producers not updated to the new schema) raises KeyError in the consumer, poisoning the batch and stalling span ingestion until offsets are skipped.

[BUG] zadd uses span.payload bytes as the sorted-set member, and within one batch the dict comprehension `{span.payload: ...}` collapses any two spans with byte-identical payloads into a single entry (score overwritten by the last). Duplicate-payload spans (identical serialized attributes, which is legal — same name/timestamp/split batches re-delivered) are silently dropped from the buffer and never flushed, losing spans from the final output.

[BUG] The new eviction path zpopmin's the lowest-score (oldest end_timestamp) members whenever the set exceeds 1000, permanently deleting those spans from the buffer with no metric, log, or flush. On high-volume traces exceeding 1000 spans per set, older spans are silently discarded and never written to storage — unbounded trace fan-out now causes unreported data loss rather than the previous explicit too-large-segment skip path.

[BUG] The redirect-chain loop limit was cut from 10000 to 1000 while deleting the comment that documented the tradeoff, with no handling for chains longer than 1000. Legitimate redirect chains deeper than 1000 (previously joined, even if slowly) now terminate the loop with set_span_id unresolved, so spans attach to the wrong segment parent — a silent correctness regression for deep traces.

[BUG] The max_segment_spans guard was deleted, leaving only the byte-size cap, so a segment composed of many tiny spans now accumulates without any span-count bound. A segment with millions of one-byte-ish payloads stays under max_segment_bytes and is materialized fully in payloads[key], creating unbounded memory materialization in the flusher where the previous code skipped the segment by count.

[ADVISORY] The `cast(SpanEvent, rapidjson.loads(...))` asserts a schema type that does not carry `end_timestamp_precise`, making the cast a lie rather than validation. Type-checkers and future readers are told the payload matches ingest_spans_v1.SpanEvent while the code reads a field absent from that type; the schema and the reader will drift without any compile-time or runtime signal.

[ADVISORY] A new behavior-changing raw query parameter `optimized_pagination` gates the alternate code path with no feature flag or options entry. The untested alternate paginator path can be toggled by any caller passing ?optimized_pagination=true (subject to the permission check), and cannot be disabled in production without a code deploy.

[ADVISORY] Using end_timestamp_precise (a float) as the zset score conflates ordering with identity: equal timestamps lose member ordering, and float precision limits distinguishable sub-microsecond timestamps. Spans sharing an end timestamp have nondeterministic zscan order, so flush output ordering for same-timestamp spans changes versus the prior set insertion order, degrading downstream span-tree reconstruction.

[BUG] OptimizedCursorPaginator subclasses BasePaginator but calls self.max_limit, self.key, self.build_queryset, self.count_hits, self.post_query_filter, and self.desc, which are attributes/methods of CursorPaginator, not BasePaginator, so any request with optimized_pagination=true crashes with AttributeError instead of paginating. Every audit-log request that activates the new 'optimized' path returns a 500; the feature the diff adds has never been executable as written.

[BUG] The negative-offset branch slices queryset with a negative start index (queryset[start_offset:stop] with start_offset < 0), which Django ORM forbids (AssertionError: 'Negative indexing is not supported'), so any advanced-features request with a negative cursor offset raises instead of returning data. The advertised 'negative offset support' path 500s on first use; the comment claiming 'the underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically' is factually wrong and the code was never run against this path.

[BUG] process_batch now requires val["end_timestamp_precise"] with no default, so any Kafka span message produced before this deploy (or by an old producer during a rolling deploy) that lacks the field crashes the consumer with KeyError. Rolling-deploy skew: old producers and new consumers cannot coexist; every pre-upgrade message in the ingest-spans topic raises KeyError and stalls/blocks partition processing until offsets are skipped or the field is backfilled.

[BUG] The redirect-depth loop limit was silently cut from 10000 to 1000, so traces with parent-chain redirects deeper than 1000 now fail to join their segment tree, whereas the previous code (which documented this exact tradeoff in the removed comment) handled up to 10000. Deep traces that previously merged correctly will stop joining, dropping subsegment linkage, with no metric or error to reveal the regression — an unaccepted behavioral regression hidden inside a 'performance optimization' PR.

[BUG] The eviction path (zpopmin when span_count > 1000) silently deletes the oldest span payloads from the buffered segment, replacing the previous explicit 'too large segment' skip-and-metric behavior in _load_segment_data with silent data loss at insert time. For segments exceeding 1000 spans, older spans are permanently evicted before flush, so flushed trace data is silently incomplete; the deleted max_segment_spans guard and its 'segment_span_count_exceeded' metric in buffer.py mean operators lose both the data and the signal that limits were hit, without explicit human acceptance of the data-loss tradeoff.

[ADVISORY] The audit-log pagination change is unrelated to the PR's stated intent ('Optimize spans buffer insertion with eviction during insert') and is gated on a raw query parameter (optimized_pagination == "true") with no feature flag or options entry. Objective drift without explicit human acceptance: an unrelated API behavior change rides in a spans-performance PR; because it is enabled per-request by any superuser/global-access member with no kill switch, it cannot be disabled without a code deploy once it misbehaves in production.

[ADVISORY] OptimizedCursorPaginator duplicates nearly the entire body of CursorPaginator.get_result (offset/extra handling, prev trimming, build_cursor call) with only the negative-offset branch differing, a copy rather than a reuse of the existing paginator. Two near-identical pagination implementations now must be kept in sync; the next fix to cursor edge handling in CursorPaginator will silently miss this copy, and the duplicate already drifts (BasePaginator base class choice is wrong for the attributes it uses).

[ADVISORY] The max_segment_spans span-count guard and its segment_span_count_exceeded metric were deleted from _load_segment_data on the assumption the Lua-side eviction caps count at 1000, but the flush path loads from segment keys whose size the new code no longer bounds in span count anywhere. If any code path populates a set_key without going through add-buffer.lua (or a partially applied deploy mixes old sadd writers with new zset readers), the flusher can again load unbounded span counts with no guard or metric, reintroducing the memory-excitation scenario the deleted check protected against.

[ADVISORY] span_count is assigned from zunionstore only inside the two conditional branches; when neither branch fires the code falls back to a separate zcard(set_key) call, adding an extra Redis round-trip on every non-merging insert (the common case) that the old sadd path did not have. The stated goal is insert-path optimization, yet every plain span insert now pays an extra zcard call per write, a hot-path regression on the exact path the PR claims to speed up.

[BUG] The new 'advanced' branch in OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result slices the queryset with an unvalidated, client-controlled negative cursor offset (queryset[start_offset:stop]), which Django QuerySets do not support. An authenticated admin-tier user sends ?optimized_pagination=true&cursor=0:-1:1 (the cursor wire format carries value:offset:is_prev, and cursors.py explicitly accepts negative offsets); Django raises AssertionError ('Negative indexing is not supported') on queryset[start_offset:stop], returning a 500 instead of a 4xx and letting any caller trip repeated expensive failed queries on a high-volume audit endpoint; the code comment 'the underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically' is factually wrong — Django raises.

[ADVISORY] The new high-volume pagination mode is enabled by a raw, unflagged query parameter gated only on is_superuser/has_global_access, with the safety argument ('permissions are checked at the queryset level') asserted in comments rather than enforced for the negative-offset feature itself. Any user can supply optimized_pagination=true and reach the admin-gated code path's parameter handling; because the negative-offset branch has no independent validation (see the 500-on-negative-slice defect), the trust boundary for this 'advanced' feature is a single boolean check plus a hope — a future non-admin endpoint reusing OptimizedCursorPaginator with enable_advanced_features defaults would expose the unvalidated-offset path to all users silently.

[ADVISORY] Every updated test uses the identical end_timestamp_precise=1700000000.0 for all spans, so the new zset-score semantics (ordering by score, zadd dedup/updating on duplicate payload, zunionstore max-score merge, and the zpopmin eviction path) are never exercised with distinct or colliding scores. A regression in score handling — e.g. zadd overwriting a member's score when the same payload bytes appear with a different timestamp, or zpopmin evicting the wrong (newest instead of oldest) spans — would pass this suite, since the tests only check membership, not which spans survive or in what order; production data loss via eviction would not be caught.

[ADVISORY] The diff deletes the max_segment_spans overflow guard from _load_segment_data (src/sentry/spans/buffer.py, the removed 'len(payloads[key]) > self.max_segment_spans' branch with its del/metrics/logger path), and the modified tests in test_buffer.py and test_flusher.py still only feed segments far below that bound, so neither the removed skip-and-delete behavior nor the new unbounded-accumulation behavior is asserted anywhere in the diff. A regression in the modified loop (e.g. cursor never reaching 0, or payloads growing past memory assumptions now that the count cap is gone) passes CI silently; the metrics.incr('spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded') path is now unreachable dead behavior that no test pins either its presence or its removal.

[ADVISORY] The consumer test only adds end_timestamp_precise to the happy-path event, but the diff changed the field from optional to required (val["end_timestamp_precise"] now raises KeyError), and no test in the diff feeds a span event lacking that key. If any producer in the wild still emits the old schema without end_timestamp_precise, process_batch crashes with KeyError on every batch and the consumer stalls, while the diff's test suite stays green — the failure mode the required-key change introduces is exactly the one untested.

[ADVISORY] The flusher test constructs all four Spans with the same now value for end_timestamp_precise, mirroring the buffer tests' single-score table, so the flush path never sees spans whose zset scores (end timestamps) differ or are out of insertion order. Any ordering assumption introduced by the set→zset migration (e.g. flusher or loader relying on zscan score order instead of the previous set's unordered sscan) is unverified; a regression that truncates or reorders flushed spans by score would pass these tests.

[BUG] The consumer now reads val["end_timestamp_precise"] with a hard subscript, so any Kafka message produced by an old producer (pre-deploy messages still in the partition backlog, or pods not yet upgraded during a rolling deploy) lacks the key and raises KeyError. During rollout, new consumer pods crash (or the batch is dead-lettered/dropped depending on the arroyo policy) on every legacy message, halting span ingestion until the backlog is drained or all producers are upgraded; spans in those batches are lost. There is no migration/backfill or backward-compatible read (val.get) for this field.

[BUG] The script switches span-buf:s:* keys from Redis sets to zsets (sadd->zadd, scard->zcard, sunionstore->zunionstore, sscan->zscan) with no migration or version gate, so during a rolling deploy old workers write sets with SADD while new workers call ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE on the same keys. Redis returns WRONGTYPE for every zcard/zunionstore/zscan executed against a key that an old-code worker created as a set, crashing the Lua script and the new consumers/flushers for those traces until the set keys expire; buffered spans behind those keys are never flushed (data loss).

[BUG] The flusher's max_segment_spans guard was deleted along with the sscan->zscan conversion, so _load_segment_data now accumulates an unbounded number of spans into payloads[key] with no cap. A segment with millions of buffered spans is loaded entirely into memory in one flush iteration, causing OOM of the flusher process and loss of all in-flight buffered spans it was processing.

[BUG] The new zpopmin eviction permanently discards the oldest buffered spans (lowest end_timestamp_precise scores) once a segment exceeds 1000 members, and those evicted payloads are never flushed downstream. Silent data loss: for high-volume traces, spans silently vanish from flushed trace data with no metric or dead-letter path; the dropped spans were already accepted into the buffer and are never written to the store.

[ADVISORY] The redirect-chain loop limit was cut from 10000 to 1000 with no comment or rationale; traces whose redirect chain legitimately exceeds depth 1000 now silently fail to join to the correct segment. Spans from very deep chains are attached to a wrong or dangling segment set, producing incorrect trace assembly — a behavioral narrowing bundled invisibly into a 'performance' PR that no test covers.

[ADVISORY] The pre-existing CursorPaginator.get_result was changed to allow negative offsets for prev cursors (start_offset = offset when cursor.is_prev), changing behavior of every existing endpoint that uses this paginator, not just the new optimized path. For a prev cursor with a large offset, queryset[offset:stop] with negative offset silently shifts the window instead of raising, returning wrong pages for all existing consumers of DateTimePaginator-based pagination; this unrelated behavior change rides along in the diff with no test.

[BUG] enable_advanced is computed unconditionally as `request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access`, and organization_context.member is None for non-member/anonymous users, so every GET raises AttributeError. Any request from a user who is not a member of the organization (including anonymous) crashes with AttributeError('NoneType' object has no attribute 'has_global_access'), returning a 500 instead of the 403/404 the endpoint contract promises — this fires on the default path, not just when optimized_pagination=true.

[BUG] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor/math.ceil on the key value unconditionally, but the audit-logs endpoint uses order_by='-datetime', so the value is a datetime object and math.ceil(datetime) raises TypeError. Every optimized_pagination=true request from an authorized admin 500s with TypeError in get_item_key (invoked both directly and via build_cursor), so the optimized path is entirely broken for the only endpoint that uses it.

[BUG] The negative-offset branch slices the Django queryset with a negative start (`queryset[cursor.offset:stop]`), which Django does not support — QuerySet slicing raises AssertionError for negative starts, contradicting the comment that the ORM 'handles negative slicing automatically'. An admin supplying a cursor with a negative offset (or any client reusing a persisted cursor after this change) gets a 500 AssertionError instead of a 4xx; the advanced-features path is unreachable-safe only by luck.

[BUG] process_batch now requires val["end_timestamp_precise"] with no .get fallback, so any span message produced without that field raises KeyError and fails the whole processing batch. During a rolling deploy, old ingesters still producing messages without end_timestamp_precise cause the process consumer to raise on every batch containing such a message, stalling the partition (poison-message crash loop) rather than skipping the span.

[ADVISORY] Eviction via zpopmin silently drops spans with no metric or log, so data loss is reported as success at the ingestion layer. When a segment exceeds 1000 spans, the oldest spans are permanently discarded before flush; operators have no signal that eviction is occurring or at what rate, so a misbehaving trace pattern loses span data invisibly (recon715 would look like missing spans, not an incident).

[ADVISORY] zunionstore aggregates duplicate members by summing their scores, so a span payload present in both set_key and span_key/parent_key gets a doubled end_timestamp score. Distorted scores corrupt the eviction ordering — a span with a doubled (future) timestamp is treated as newest and never evicted while correctly-scored older spans are popped, so the wrong spans are dropped under eviction pressure.

[ADVISORY] The redirect-chain loop limit was cut from 10000 to 1000, silently changing which deep parent chains fail to join. Traces with redirect chains deeper than 1000 now stop resolving mid-chain with no log or metric distinguishing 'hit the new limit' from 'chain terminated normally', producing silently partial segment joins for exactly the pathological traces the old limit tolerated.

[ADVISORY] The max_segment_spans guard (count-based skip of oversized segments) was deleted, leaving only the byte-size cap. A segment composed of many tiny spans can now accumulate an unbounded span count per flush page as long as each zscan page stays under max_segment_bytes; flush payload size and downstream flusher work are no longer bounded by count, and the segment_span_count_exceeded signal is gone so the new behavior is unobservable.

[ADVISORY] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result duplicates ~60 lines of CursorPaginator.get_result with only the offset branch differing. Two hand-maintained copies of the cursor-advance/prev-trim logic will drift on the next paginator fix (the diff itself already introduces drift: base get_result clamps offsets with max(0, offset) while this copy does not in its else branch is fine, but prev-trim arithmetic `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` is wrong when offset is negative), so a future bugfix to one silently misses the other.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] zadd uses span.payload bytes as the sorted-set member, and within one batch the dict comprehension `{span.payload: ...}` collapses any two spans with byte-identical payloads into a single entry (score overwritten by the last). adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new eviction path zpopmin's the lowest-score (oldest end_timestamp) members whenever the set exceeds 1000, permanently deleting those spans from the buffer with no metric, log, or flush. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The redirect-chain loop limit was cut from 10000 to 1000 while deleting the comment that documented the tradeoff, with no handling for chains longer than 1000. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The max_segment_spans guard was deleted, leaving only the byte-size cap, so a segment composed of many tiny spans now accumulates without any span-count bound. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The eviction path (zpopmin when span_count > 1000) silently deletes the oldest span payloads from the buffered segment, replacing the previous explicit 'too large segment' skip-and-metric behavior in _load_segment_data with silent data loss at insert time. For segments exceeding 1000 spans, older spans are permanently evicted before flush, so flushed trace data is silently incomplete; the deleted max_segment_spans guard and its 'segment_span_count_exceeded' metric in buffer.py mean operators lose both the data and the signal that limits were hit, without explicit human acceptance of the data-loss tradeoff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] OptimizedCursorPaginator duplicates nearly the entire body of CursorPaginator.get_result (offset/extra handling, prev trimming, build_cursor call) with only the negative-offset branch differing, a copy rather than a reuse of the existing paginator. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The max_segment_spans span-count guard and its segment_span_count_exceeded metric were deleted from _load_segment_data on the assumption the Lua-side eviction caps count at 1000, but the flush path loads from segment keys whose size the new code no longer bounds in span count anywhere. The new write path in `process_spans` now uses `ZADD` directly (`p.zadd(set_key, {span.payload: span.end_timestamp_precise ...})`) with no trimming, while the only count cap shown (`zpopmin` to 1000) exists in `add-buffer.lua` and is not applied to these `process_spans` writes. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] span_count is assigned from zunionstore only inside the two conditional branches; when neither branch fires the code falls back to a separate zcard(set_key) call, adding an extra Redis round-trip on every non-merging insert (the common case) that the old sadd path did not have. The stated goal is insert-path optimization, yet every plain span insert now pays an extra zcard call per write, a hot-path regression on the exact path the PR claims to speed up.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua`, `span_count` is initialized to 0 and only set when either `zunionstore` branch executes. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new 'advanced' branch in OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result slices the queryset with an unvalidated, client-controlled negative cursor offset (queryset[start_offset:stop]), which Django QuerySets do not support. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Every updated test uses the identical end_timestamp_precise=1700000000.0 for all spans, so the new zset-score semantics (ordering by score, zadd dedup/updating on duplicate payload, zunionstore max-score merge, and the zpopmin eviction path) are never exercised with distinct or colliding scores. A regression in score handling — e.g. zadd overwriting a member's score when the same payload bytes appear with a different timestamp, or zpopmin evicting the wrong (newest instead of oldest) spans — would pass this suite, since the tests only check membership, not which spans survive or in what order; production data loss via eviction would not be caught.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes span buffering from Redis sets to sorted sets: `zadd(... {span.payload: span.end_timestamp_precise})` in `SpansBuffer.process_spans`, `zscan` replaces `sscan`, and `add-buffer.lua` now merges with `zunionstore` and may evict with `zpopmin` when `span_count > 1000`. The updated/added tests in the diff set `end_timestamp_precise` to a constant `1700000000.0` (or `now`) for all spans, so they do not exercise any behavior that depends on varying scores (ordering/oldest-vs-newest semantics) or score updates/collisions for the same member payload. This is a concrete gap in coverage for the newly introduced zset-score semantics and eviction logic, but it is not itself a defect in the implementation shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The diff deletes the max_segment_spans overflow guard from _load_segment_data (src/sentry/spans/buffer.py, the removed 'len(payloads[key]) > self.max_segment_spans' branch with its del/metrics/logger path), and the modified tests in test_buffer.py and test_flusher.py still only feed segments far below that bound, so neither the removed skip-and-delete behavior nor the new unbounded-accumulation behavior is asserted anywhere in the diff. A regression in the modified loop (e.g. cursor never reaching 0, or payloads growing past memory assumptions now that the count cap is gone) passes CI silently; the metrics.incr('spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded') path is now unreachable dead behavior that no test pins either its presence or its removal.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the span-count overflow guard in `SpansBuffer._load_segment_data` (the `if len(payloads[key]) > self.max_segment_spans:` branch with `metrics.incr("spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded")` and deletion of `payloads[key]/cursors[key]` is deleted). Tests updated in `tests/sentry/spans/test_buffer.py` and `test_flusher.py` only add small numbers of spans and do not exercise any overflow/large-segment behavior. While Redis-side changes (switch to zsets + Lua `zpopmin` cap at 1000) may be intended to bound size, this nontrivial behavioral shift (Python-side drop-on-overflow vs. Redis-side trimming) is not pinned by tests, so regressions in paging/termination or unexpected memory growth wouldn’t be caught by CI.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The consumer test only adds end_timestamp_precise to the happy-path event, but the diff changed the field from optional to required (val["end_timestamp_precise"] now raises KeyError), and no test in the diff feeds a span event lacking that key. If any producer in the wild still emits the old schema without end_timestamp_precise, process_batch crashes with KeyError on every batch and the consumer stalls, while the diff's test suite stays green — the failure mode the required-key change introduces is exactly the one untested.

adjudication.rationale: In `process_batch` the span construction now unconditionally reads `end_timestamp_precise=val["end_timestamp_precise"]` (previously this key was not required at all), and `Span` was changed to require this field (no default). If an incoming event payload lacks `end_timestamp_precise`, this will raise `KeyError` and break batch processing. The updated tests only cover events that include the key, so this crash path is untested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The flusher test constructs all four Spans with the same now value for end_timestamp_precise, mirroring the buffer tests' single-score table, so the flush path never sees spans whose zset scores (end timestamps) differ or are out of insertion order. Any ordering assumption introduced by the set→zset migration (e.g. flusher or loader relying on zscan score order instead of the previous set's unordered sscan) is unverified; a regression that truncates or reorders flushed spans by score would pass these tests.

adjudication.rationale: The diff migrates span buffering from Redis sets to sorted sets (buffer.py uses ZADD with score=span.end_timestamp_precise; loader switches SSCAN→ZSCAN; Lua uses ZUNIONSTORE and trims with ZPOPMIN based on score). However, the updated tests (e.g. tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_flusher.py) set end_timestamp_precise to the same `now` value for all spans, and buffer tests similarly use a single constant score. This means the test suite never exercises differing zset scores or insertion-order-vs-score interactions, so a score-dependent regression in trimming/iteration (e.g., ZPOPMIN removing unexpected spans, or relying on ZSCAN iteration characteristics) could slip through unverified.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The consumer now reads val["end_timestamp_precise"] with a hard subscript, so any Kafka message produced by an old producer (pre-deploy messages still in the partition backlog, or pods not yet upgraded during a rolling deploy) lacks the key and raises KeyError. During rollout, new consumer pods crash (or the batch is dead-lettered/dropped depending on the arroyo policy) on every legacy message, halting span ingestion until the backlog is drained or all producers are upgraded; spans in those batches are lost. There is no migration/backfill or backward-compatible read (val.get) for this field.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/factory.py`, the consumer now does `end_timestamp_precise=val["end_timestamp_precise"]` after `rapidjson.loads(...)`. This is a hard subscript that will raise `KeyError` if the decoded message lacks that field. The diff shows this field was newly added (tests updated to include it), and there is no backward-compatible `val.get(...)` / defaulting logic, so legacy messages without the key would break processing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The script switches span-buf:s:* keys from Redis sets to zsets (sadd->zadd, scard->zcard, sunionstore->zunionstore, sscan->zscan) with no migration or version gate, so during a rolling deploy old workers write sets with SADD while new workers call ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE on the same keys. Redis returns WRONGTYPE for every zcard/zunionstore/zscan executed against a key that an old-code worker created as a set, crashing the Lua script and the new consumers/flushers for those traces until the set keys expire; buffered spans behind those keys are never flushed (data loss).

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the Redis data structure for the existing key namespace `span-buf:s:{...}:...` from SETs to ZSETs: `buffer.py` switches `sadd`->`zadd` and `sscan`->`zscan`, and `add-buffer.lua` switches `scard`/`sunionstore` to `zcard`/`zunionstore` and adds `zpopmin`. The key format is unchanged, and there is no migration, version gate, or fallback handling in either the Python code or the Lua script for keys that may already exist as SETs. In a rolling deploy, old code can create/populate SET keys while new code performs ZSET operations on the same keys, which in Redis results in `WRONGTYPE` errors and would break buffering/flush behavior for those traces until expiration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The flusher's max_segment_spans guard was deleted along with the sscan->zscan conversion, so _load_segment_data now accumulates an unbounded number of spans into payloads[key] with no cap. A segment with millions of buffered spans is loaded entirely into memory in one flush iteration, causing OOM of the flusher process and loss of all in-flight buffered spans it was processing.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpansBuffer._load_segment_data` the previous span-count cap was removed when switching `sscan` to `zscan`. The diff deletes the block that checked `if len(payloads[key]) > self.max_segment_spans: ... skip segment` and now always does `payloads[key].extend(span for span, _ in zscan_values)` while continuing to scan until `cursor == 0` (or until `max_segment_bytes` is exceeded). This means there is no longer an explicit bound on the number of spans accumulated per segment in memory during a flush, so a large Redis sorted set could cause very large in-memory lists and potential OOM as the finding describes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new zpopmin eviction permanently discards the oldest buffered spans (lowest end_timestamp_precise scores) once a segment exceeds 1000 members, and those evicted payloads are never flushed downstream. Silent data loss: for high-volume traces, spans silently vanish from flushed trace data with no metric or dead-letter path; the dropped spans were already accepted into the buffer and are never written to the store.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an explicit hard cap in `add-buffer.lua`: after merging spans into the per-segment sorted set (`zunionstore`), it computes `span_count` and, if `span_count > 1000`, calls `zpopmin(set_key, span_count - 1000)` which removes the lowest-score members (oldest `end_timestamp_precise`). Those removed payloads are deleted from Redis and therefore cannot be read later by `_load_segment_data` (now using `zscan`) and cannot be flushed downstream. The previous Python-side protection for too many spans (`max_segment_spans` check with metric/error and skipping the entire segment) was removed, so this new eviction is silent (no metric/log in the diff) and results in accepted buffered spans being dropped.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The redirect-chain loop limit was cut from 10000 to 1000 with no comment or rationale; traces whose redirect chain legitimately exceeds depth 1000 now silently fail to join to the correct segment. Spans from very deep chains are attached to a wrong or dangling segment set, producing incorrect trace assembly — a behavioral narrowing bundled invisibly into a 'performance' PR that no test covers.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua`, the redirect-chain resolution loop limit is reduced from `for i = 0, 10000 do` (with an explicit comment about depth) to `for i = 0, 1000 do` with no compensating handling when the loop hits the cap. If a redirect chain exceeds 1000, the loop will terminate without reaching the `break` condition (`not new_set_span or new_set_span == set_span_id`), and the code will proceed to `hset`/merge using whatever intermediate `set_span_id` it last saw, potentially attaching spans to an incorrect/dangling segment set. This is a behavior-narrowing correctness risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The pre-existing CursorPaginator.get_result was changed to allow negative offsets for prev cursors (start_offset = offset when cursor.is_prev), changing behavior of every existing endpoint that uses this paginator, not just the new optimized path. For a prev cursor with a large offset, queryset[offset:stop] with negative offset silently shifts the window instead of raising, returning wrong pages for all existing consumers of DateTimePaginator-based pagination; this unrelated behavior change rides along in the diff with no test.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/api/paginator.py`, the only functional change in the existing `get_result` path is that **non-prev** cursors clamp `offset` to `>= 0` via `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`. For `cursor.is_prev`, the code still uses `offset` exactly as before (previously it sliced `queryset[offset:stop]` directly), so the diff does not introduce a new “allow negative offsets for prev cursors” behavior. The finding’s claim about wrong pages for existing DateTimePaginator consumers due to a new negative-offset prev behavior is therefore not grounded in the diff (and no new negative-offset logic is added to the legacy path beyond this clamp for non-prev).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] enable_advanced is computed unconditionally as `request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access`, and organization_context.member is None for non-member/anonymous users, so every GET raises AttributeError. Any request from a user who is not a member of the organization (including anonymous) crashes with AttributeError('NoneType' object has no attribute 'has_global_access'), returning a 500 instead of the 403/404 the endpoint contract promises — this fires on the default path, not just when optimized_pagination=true.

adjudication.rationale: In `organization_auditlogs.py`, `enable_advanced` is computed unconditionally as `request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access`. If `organization_context.member` can be `None` (e.g., user is authenticated but not an org member), and `request.user.is_superuser` is false, this will raise an `AttributeError` before the `if use_optimized and enable_advanced:` gate, affecting the non-optimized path too. The diff introduces this potential `None` dereference.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor/math.ceil on the key value unconditionally, but the audit-logs endpoint uses order_by='-datetime', so the value is a datetime object and math.ceil(datetime) raises TypeError. Every optimized_pagination=true request from an authorized admin 500s with TypeError in get_item_key (invoked both directly and via build_cursor), so the optimized path is entirely broken for the only endpoint that uses it.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` (added in `src/sentry/api/paginator.py`), `get_item_key` does `math.floor`/`math.ceil` on `value = getattr(item, self.key)` and then casts to `int`. In the only diff-shown call site enabling this paginator (`organization_auditlogs.py`), pagination is configured with `order_by="-datetime"`, implying the paginator key is the `datetime` field. Applying `math.floor`/`math.ceil` to a `datetime` object will raise `TypeError`, so the optimized path would 500 when it tries to compute cursor keys (including via `build_cursor`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The negative-offset branch slices the Django queryset with a negative start (`queryset[cursor.offset:stop]`), which Django does not support — QuerySet slicing raises AssertionError for negative starts, contradicting the comment that the ORM 'handles negative slicing automatically'. An admin supplying a cursor with a negative offset (or any client reusing a persisted cursor after this change) gets a 500 AssertionError instead of a 4xx; the advanced-features path is unreachable-safe only by luck.

adjudication.rationale: In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result`, when `enable_advanced_features` is true and `cursor.offset < 0`, it sets `start_offset = cursor.offset` and slices `queryset[start_offset:stop]` (i.e., a negative slice start). Django `QuerySet` slicing does not support negative indices and raises an `AssertionError` for negative starts, so this branch can trigger a 500 despite the comment claiming the ORM "properly handles negative slicing automatically". The diff also explicitly documents allowing negative offsets (`Cursor.offset` comment), making this reachable if a client provides such a cursor.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] process_batch now requires val["end_timestamp_precise"] with no .get fallback, so any span message produced without that field raises KeyError and fails the whole processing batch. During a rolling deploy, old ingesters still producing messages without end_timestamp_precise cause the process consumer to raise on every batch containing such a message, stalling the partition (poison-message crash loop) rather than skipping the span.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/factory.py`, `process_batch` now constructs `Span(..., end_timestamp_precise=val["end_timestamp_precise"], ...)` after `val = cast(SpanEvent, rapidjson.loads(payload.value))`. There is no `.get()`/default and no try/except, so any message lacking the `end_timestamp_precise` key will raise `KeyError` and abort processing of that batch. The diff itself does not show any compatibility handling for older producers, so the finding (rolling deploy/poison message risk) is consistent with the introduced strict indexing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Eviction via zpopmin silently drops spans with no metric or log, so data loss is reported as success at the ingestion layer. When a segment exceeds 1000 spans, the oldest spans are permanently discarded before flush; operators have no signal that eviction is occurring or at what rate, so a misbehaving trace pattern loses span data invisibly (recon715 would look like missing spans, not an incident).

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds an eviction path in `add-buffer.lua`: after unions, it computes `span_count` and if `span_count > 1000` it calls `redis.call("zpopmin", set_key, span_count - 1000)`, permanently discarding the oldest spans. There is no accompanying metric/log emission around this eviction in the Lua script, and the previous Python-side oversize handling in `_load_segment_data` (which incremented metrics/logged when span count exceeded) has been removed. So the core concern—silent span dropping with no operator signal when exceeding the 1000 cap—is diff-grounded, but it’s an observability/product tradeoff rather than a strictly verifiable “bug” given the cap appears intentional.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] zunionstore aggregates duplicate members by summing their scores, so a span payload present in both set_key and span_key/parent_key gets a doubled end_timestamp score. Distorted scores corrupt the eviction ordering — a span with a doubled (future) timestamp is treated as newest and never evicted while correctly-scored older spans are popped, so the wrong spans are dropped under eviction pressure.

adjudication.rationale: In `add-buffer.lua`, merges now use `zunionstore` (e.g. `redis.call("zunionstore", set_key, 2, set_key, span_key)`) without specifying an `AGGREGATE` option. Redis defaults to `SUM`, so if the same span payload exists in both `set_key` and `span_key`/`parent_key`, its score (here `end_timestamp_precise` as set by `zadd` in `buffer.py`) will be summed/doubled. Since eviction trims with `zpopmin` based on score (`end_timestamp_precise`), inflated scores will change ordering and can cause the wrong elements to be evicted under pressure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The redirect-chain loop limit was cut from 10000 to 1000, silently changing which deep parent chains fail to join. Traces with redirect chains deeper than 1000 now stop resolving mid-chain with no log or metric distinguishing 'hit the new limit' from 'chain terminated normally', producing silently partial segment joins for exactly the pathological traces the old limit tolerated.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua` the redirect-chain resolution loop limit is reduced from `for i = 0, 10000 do` to `for i = 0, 1000 do`. The loop sets `redirect_depth = i` but has no post-loop check for “hit max iterations”; if the chain is deeper than 1000, the loop will terminate due to the `for` bound rather than a natural break (`not new_set_span or new_set_span == set_span_id`). The code then proceeds to `hset` the redirect mapping using the unresolved (mid-chain) `set_span_id`, causing silently incomplete/incorrect joining for deep chains, with no log/metric differentiating this case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The max_segment_spans guard (count-based skip of oversized segments) was deleted, leaving only the byte-size cap. A segment composed of many tiny spans can now accumulate an unbounded span count per flush page as long as each zscan page stays under max_segment_bytes; flush payload size and downstream flusher work are no longer bounded by count, and the segment_span_count_exceeded signal is gone so the new behavior is unobservable.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the explicit span-count guard in `SpansBuffer._load_segment_data`: the block checking `if len(payloads[key]) > self.max_segment_spans: ... del payloads[key] ...` (and the associated `segment_span_count_exceeded` metric/log) was deleted, and the new code only enforces `self.max_segment_bytes` while continuing to `zscan`/`extend` payloads until the cursor is exhausted. With many tiny span payloads, the number of spans accumulated/processed per segment is no longer bounded by count in this flush path, and the prior observability signal is indeed gone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result duplicates ~60 lines of CursorPaginator.get_result with only the offset branch differing. Two hand-maintained copies of the cursor-advance/prev-trim logic will drift on the next paginator fix (the diff itself already introduces drift: base get_result clamps offsets with max(0, offset) while this copy does not in its else branch is fine, but prev-trim arithmetic `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` is wrong when offset is negative), so a future bugfix to one silently misses the other.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a code path in `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` that explicitly allows negative offsets (`start_offset = cursor.offset` when `enable_advanced_features` and `cursor.offset < 0`). However, the subsequent “prev-trim” logic still uses the original `offset` in `len(results) == offset + limit + extra`, which no longer matches how many rows were actually requested when `start_offset` is negative (the slice length is driven by `stop - start_offset`, not by `offset + limit + extra`). This makes the trimming condition incorrect for the newly-supported negative-offset path and can lead to wrong inclusion/exclusion of rows when paginating backwards.
